text: Dr. Yossi Vardi is known as Israel's 'Father of the Entrepreneur', and he has many children in the form of technology companies he has helped to incubate in Tel Aviv's booming Internet sector.

text: At the offices of Superna, one such company, he introduced a whirlwind of presentations from his baby incubators to a group of journalists.

text: What stuck most in my head was when Vardi said, "What is important is not the technology, but the talent."

text: Perhaps because he repeated this after each young Internet entrepreneur showed us his or her latest creation under Vardi's tutelage.
title: Israel Journal: Is Yossi Vardi a good father to his entrepreneurial children?

text: I had a sense of déjà vu from this mantra.
title: Israel Journal: Is Yossi Vardi a good father to his entrepreneurial children?

text: A casual reader of the newspapers during the Dot.com boom will remember a glut of stories that could be called "The Rise of the Failure"; people whose technology companies had collapsed were suddenly hot commodities to start up new companies.
title: Israel Journal: Is Yossi Vardi a good father to his entrepreneurial children?

text: This seemingly paradoxical thinking was talked about as new back then; but even Thomas Edison—the Father of Invention—is oft-quoted for saying, "I have not failed.

text: I have just found ten thousand ways that won’t work."
title: Israel Journal: Is Yossi Vardi a good father to his entrepreneurial children?

text: Vardi's focus on encouraging his brood of talent regardless of the practicalities stuck out to me because of a recent pair of "dueling studies" The New York Times has printed.
title: Israel Journal: Is Yossi Vardi a good father to his entrepreneurial children?

text: These are the sort of studies that confuse parents on how to raise their kids.
title: Israel Journal: Is Yossi Vardi a good father to his entrepreneurial children?

text: The first, by Carol Dweck at Stanford University, came to the conclusion that children who are not praised for their efforts, regardless of the outcome's success, rarely attempt more challenging and complex pursuits.
title: Israel Journal: Is Yossi Vardi a good father to his entrepreneurial children?

text: According to Dweck's study, when a child knows that they will receive praise for being right instead of for tackling difficult problems, even if they fail, they will simply elect to take on easy tasks in which they are assured of finding the solution.
title: Israel Journal: Is Yossi Vardi a good father to his entrepreneurial children?

text: Only one month earlier the Times produced another story for parents to agonize over, this time based on a study from the Brookings Institution, entitled "Are Kids Getting Too Much Praise?"
title: Israel Journal: Is Yossi Vardi a good father to his entrepreneurial children?

text: Unlike Dweck's clinical study, Brookings drew conclusions from statistical data that could be influenced by a variety of factors (since there was no clinical control).

text: That's not to say he has not found his latest ICQ, though only time—and consumers—will tell.
title: Israel Journal: Is Yossi Vardi a good father to his entrepreneurial children?

text: The United States men's ice hockey team upset host country Canada, 5-3, in a preliminary round game on Sunday at the Winter Olympics.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: It is being called the Americans' biggest Olympic win since the 1980s "Miracle on Ice" victory over the former Soviet Union.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: The game was only 41 seconds in when Brian Rafalski of Team USA fired a slap shot that deflected off Canadian star Sidney Crosby's stick and bounced past Canadian goalkeeper Martin Brodeur.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: The Canadians evened the game on a goal nearly nine minutes into the contest on Eric Staal's shot.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: The capacity crowd roared its approval and the stadium announcer was still giving the details of Staal's goal when Rafalski scored again.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Canada evened the game in the second period, but American Chris Drury put Team USA ahead again, 3-2.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: The Americans took a 4-2 lead on Jamie Langenbrunner's shot with just under 13 minutes left in the game.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Crosby cut the U.S. lead to 4-3 with about three minutes left.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Canada pulled goalie Brodeur, adding an extra attacker in a desperate attempt to tie the contest.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: The hosts had clearly outplayed the Americans, with a shot advantage of 45-23.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: But U.S. goalie Ryan Miller, frustrated the Canadians all night, including their last-ditch attack.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Then with just 45 seconds left in the contest, American Ryan Kesler reached around his opponent to slap the final U.S. goal into the empty Canadian net, making it 5-3.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: The game was just a preliminary round match, but in hockey-mad Canada, where the sport first originated, it was more than that.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: To lose to the United States in the Olympics on home soil was devastating.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: After the game, Canada fans — many in replicas of the team's red and white Maple Leaf jerseys — seemed stunned as they filed out of the Canada Hockey Place.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Some Americans chanted "U-S-A, U-S-A!"
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: But many Canadians, including Melissa Mazeman of Winnipeg, Manitoba, were still trying to realize what had happened.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: "As soon as that first goal was scored within in the first minute, that did hurt, it was kind of crushing," she said.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: "But every U.S. player — or every U.S. fan I have seen on the street — I have said congratulations [to]."
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Meanwhile, Canadian coach Mike Babcock has replaced Brodeur in the lineup, with Roberto Luongo of the Vancouver Canucks.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Babcock said Brodeur's coordination with his defensemen that led to turnovers and four goals out of 22 American shot attempts.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: He also noted that Brodeur did not make many big saves.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Babcock said, "We’re in the winning business.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: And to win at any level you need momentum-changing saves."
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Team USA fan David Loring of Colorado Springs, Colorado, one of a vastly outnumbered corps of fans wearing USA Hockey gear, gave goalkeeper Ryan Miller the credit for preserving the win.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: "[Team USA] played really well tonight.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: I have to tell you, they got outplayed by Canada.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: We had some really good goalie work this evening.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Brodeur made some nice saves, but Miller really played well tonight.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: That was the difference I thought."
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: However, not all Americans are happy.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: The general manager of the U.S. men's team, Brian Burke, feels the team isn't playing at it's best.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: "I’m not happy with the way we’ve played to this point.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: We have to play significantly better.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: We’re playing with about 10 guys carrying us.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: They don’t hand out any medals for finishing first in the preliminary round," Burke said.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: He continued saying, "Our center-ice play, we’ve made some glaring turnovers that have resulted in scoring chances.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: And our overall intensity for 60 minutes — for the first 10 minutes in the second period, I thought we were nonexistent."
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Chris Drury agreed saying, "I’d still say we would be the underdogs on our lack of experience, certainly now that the tournament takes on a whole new meaning with single elimination.
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: We do need to get a lot better."
title: USA upsets Canada in Olympic ice hockey

text: Tuggeranong, Canberra — The second day of the Australian National Archery Championships was underway today at the Tuggeranong Archery Club in Canberra, with the field shooting competition being one of the highlights, as Australians in several bow classes were attempting to qualify for the World Archery Field Championships in August.

text: Archery fights to stay on the Olympic programme because of low spectator numbers and one of the smaller participation bases.
title: Australian field archers vie for spot at World Championships

text: London, England — With the 2012 Summer Paralympics starting in less than a week, parts of Papua New Guinea's Paralympic delegation arrived in London earlier today in order to support the pair of athletes the country qualified for the Games, athletics competitor Francis Kompaon and powerlifter Timothy Harabe.
title: Papua New Guinea represented by two Paralympians in London

title: Papua New Guinea represented by two Paralympians in London

text: Harabe, only the tenth person ever to represent his country at the Games, is making his Paralympic Games debut.
title: Papua New Guinea represented by two Paralympians in London

text: The British High Commissioner to Papua New Guinea, Jackie Barson, MBE, wished both athletes well, saying in a written statement, "It is a fantastic achievement for the PNG to be represented by two world class Paralympic athletes".
title: Papua New Guinea represented by two Paralympians in London

text: PNG Paralympic Committee President Bernard Chan also congratulated his country's athletes, saying, "They will be great ambassadors for PNG and I hope both Francis and Timothy will inspire other athletes to train hard and hope to represent PNG at this Paralympic level during their participation."
title: Papua New Guinea represented by two Paralympians in London

text: The 2012 Games will be the fourth time the country has participated, with the three other appearances happening at the 1984 Summer Paralympics, 2000 Summer Paralympics and 2008 Summer Paralympics.
title: Papua New Guinea represented by two Paralympians in London

text: Other members of the Papua New Guinea 2012 Paralympic delegation include PNG Paralympic Committee President Bernard Chan; Chef de Mission Dr. Kefu Ma; team manager Rosemary Mawe; Davina Chan, the president's wife; coach William McKenny; and official Jeffrey Robby.
title: Papua New Guinea represented by two Paralympians in London

text: In the 18 months since Andrea Muizelaar was crowned winner of the reality TV series Canada's Next Top Model, her life has been a complete whirlwind.

title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: Andrea Muizelaar: I am from Whitby, Ontario.
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: My Dad works in the nuclear industry and my Mom is a stay-at-home mom.
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: I had a lot of trouble from my peers at school due to my "geeky" appearance - braces, etc.

text: Worse than any other teenager?
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: AM: Probably not extremely geeky; more of being a victim of a bully who liked to pick on me continuously and influenced other kids to do likewise.
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: MH: How long did that last?
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: AM: I would say from Grade 2 to Grade 9.
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: MH: What happened after that point?
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: AM: I definitely grew into my looks, the braces came off; high school is a bigger place and the bullying subsided because I had new friends.
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: Did they have that thin body type that you hoped to have?
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: AM: I looked up to anyone in a media image as well as, and especially, America's Next Top Model contestants.
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: MH: That was actually going to be my next question.
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: Who did you look up to on that show?
title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

title: Andrea Muizelaar on fashion, anorexia, and life after 'Top Model'

text: AM: Like most of the viewers of the show, I had no idea where any of the winners or past-contestants ended up.

text: Now, I am starting to rebuild my career more than anyone ever helped me to before...and to boot...I am healthy doing it.

text: A multi-center US study of 748 patients, who were to undergo treatment for coronary artery disease, has found that prayer by Christian, Muslim, Jewish, and Buddhist groups had no measurable effects on the medical health of the study subjects.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: The prayers were conducted by established congregations and were held away from the hospitals.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: The study, published in the 16 July 2005 issue of The Lancet, found that the likelihood of an adverse cardiovascular event in hospital, re-admission or death within six months was unaffected by prayer.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: None of the patients were told that they were prayed for, and none of the prayer groups knew who they prayed for.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: Nevertheless, 67% of the non-prayer group believed they were being prayed for - a potential placebo effect that may have hidden any small differences between the two groups.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: The study also examined the effects of "music, imagery, and touch (MIT) therapy" before heart surgery.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: Practitioners qualified to Level 1 Healing Touch taught the patient relaxation techniques and played soothing music before applying 21 Healing Touch hand positions, over a 40 minute session.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: There was no significant change in the combined chance of an adverse cardiovascular event in hospital, re-admission or death within six months.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: However, while the set of patients was evenly split, only 7 patients who received MIT therapy died, and 20 patients who did not receive it died.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: The result is not highly significant due to the low overall number of people who died.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: A number of studies has recently examined the possible effects of prayer, with mixed results.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: While some religious groups have hailed studies which found positive results [1], skeptics have challenged the very notion of scientifically examining prayer [2], and have described past studies as flawed or even fraudulent.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: "The mechanisms through which distant intercessory prayer might convey healing benefit are unknown", the authors of the study explain.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: One hypothesis they propose for such effects are "non-local features of consciousness based theoretically around observations in quantum physics."
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: The study was conducted by a team of 16 researchers at Duke Clinical Research Institute (DCRI), Duke University Medical Center, the Durham Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC), and seven other academic medical institutions across the United States.
title: Prayer does not help heart patients, study finds

text: The New York Times reports that safety officials working for the Food and Drug Administration have expressed concerns over the safety of an antibiotic, telithromycin and questioned its approval for use.

text: The drug, marketed under the trade name Ketek, has been widely prescribed since its 2004 FDA approval.

text: The New York Times reports that David Graham, one of four FDA safety officials concerned about safety of the antibiotic in both adults and children, wrote in an E-mail message to another agency official that the drug's 2004 U.S. approval was in error and should be withdrawn.
title: FDA officials question safety of antibiotic 'Ketek'

text: The concerns focus on the drug's liver toxicity, but also extends to vision problems and other nervous system effects (reported blackouts) and worsening of symptoms in patients suffering from myasthenia gravis.
title: FDA officials question safety of antibiotic 'Ketek'

text: The drug has been prescribed more than 5 million times.
title: FDA officials question safety of antibiotic 'Ketek'

text: Liver failure has been reported in fourteen adult patients, four of whom died; another twenty-three sustained "serious liver injury."
title: FDA officials question safety of antibiotic 'Ketek'

text: In January 2006, after cases of serious liver toxicity were reported in the Annals of Internal Medicine (a professional journal published by the American Medical Association), the FDA issued a public advisory to that effect and, in June, 2006 announced that it had completed its safety assessment and required the manufacturer to add additional warnings about the risks of liver toxicity and for patients with myasthenia gravis to the product labeling.
title: FDA officials question safety of antibiotic 'Ketek'

text: An F.D.A. spokeswoman, Susan Bro, said, “Every issue or question raised during the Ketek review process and subsequently since approval has been rigorously reviewed by the nation’s best physicians, statisticians and epidemiologists both internal and external to the F.D.A.”

text: Researchers have found a crucial genetic difference between humans and chimps that could help explain our language and speech abilities.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: The difference lies in a gene called FOXP2 which encodes for a protein of the same name.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: This acts as a transcription factor, controlling the activity of other genes.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: The human and chimp versions of the protein differ in only two of their 740 amino acid components, but when researchers at the University of California, Los Angeles, replaced the human gene with the chimp version in neurons grown in the laboratory, they found it affected the expression of at least 116 other genes.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: The results are detailed in a paper published on Thursday in the scientific journal Nature.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: Author of the study Dr. Daniel Geschwind, of the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA, said the gene had a "major role" in differences between chimps and humans.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: "We showed that the human and chimp versions of FOXP2 not only look different but function differently too."
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: Some of the affected genes control the formation of connections in the brain, whilst others relate to facial movements.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: Several have already been found to be involved in language disorders.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: Mutations in FOXP2 itself were also known to affect speech and language; the gene was first identified in members of a family suffering from language problems who were found to share a genetic mutation.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: Frances Vargha-Khadem at University College London has studied patients with FOXP2 mutations, and agrees with the new research.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: As well as language problems, some of her subjects have changes in the shape of their jaws, mouths and tongues.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: She thinks that chimps may also have these differences.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: "We believe FOXP2 is not only important for the higher order cognitive aspect of language but also for the motor aspect of speech and language," said Genevieve Konopka, one of the authors of the paper at UCLA.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: Previous research indicates that the changes in FOXP2 occurred around 200,000 years ago with the rise of modern humans.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: Geschwind also suggests that several of the related genes may have evolved together.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: Preliminary studies have shown signs that they too emerged relatively recently.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: Scientists are now keen to further study FOXP2 and the genes that it affects.
title: Scientists find key human language gene

text: Geschwind believes this could eventually lead to breakthroughs in treatment for disorders such as autism and schizophrenia, which affect language skills.

text: UNICEF published a new report titled, "THE STATE OF THE WORLD’S CHILDREN 2012 — Children in an Urban World".

text: About one billion children and adolescents, and thus half of all children and adolescents, are living in cities.
title: UNICEF: An increasing number of children are living in slums

text: The continuing urbanization makes the cities of the world grow annually by about 60 million people.
title: UNICEF: An increasing number of children are living in slums

text: The needs and rights of children and adolescents are, according to UNICEF, often disregarded and play no significant role in urban planning.
title: UNICEF: An increasing number of children are living in slums

text: In order to give children a voice in urban decision-making processes, UNICEF has worked on the Child-Friendly Cities Initiative.
title: UNICEF: An increasing number of children are living in slums

text: The report describes the effects of poverty with regard to malnutrition, poor hygiene, educational inequality and vulnerability; social inequality also leads to crime and violence.
title: UNICEF: An increasing number of children are living in slums

text: The infant mortality in poor slums is higher than in some rural areas.
title: UNICEF: An increasing number of children are living in slums

text: Often between 50 and 80 percent of the income of a family are required for nutrition and access to existing health services; in the cities this is not possible, so diseases such as measles, tuberculosis and other diseases avoidable by vaccination are becoming dangerously prevalent again.
title: UNICEF: An increasing number of children are living in slums

text: Following a similar experiment in 2009, six men entered an enclosed room in Moscow last Thursday to simulate a flight to Mars.

text: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) posted a press release on its website yesterday stating it will identify up to six banks as domestic systemically important banks (D-SIB), which would be equivalent to the too big to fail banks of other nations.

text: Several commemoration ceremonies were recently held for victims of the Great Hanshin earthquake of 1995, mainly in Kansai region.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: The municipality of Kobe and supporting organisations held one such ceremony in the early morning of January 17.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: It was the biggest ceremony held that day.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Over 5,000 people gathered in the East Playground in the center of city.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Participants included surviving citizens and volunteers from around the whole country who had helped out.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: At 5:43 a.m., just 10 years after the earthquake first occurred, people lit candles in honor of the 6,433 victims.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: The victims included 133 people who died in the aftermath of the disaster, due to physical or mental difficulties caused by the heavy changes in their life.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: The earthquake centered around Awaji Island, near the city of Kobe.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: It measured 7.3 on the Richter Scale, the biggest quake to hit Japan since World War II.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Though a great earthquake could theoretically occur in any part of Japan, and scientists had warned of the possibility of earthquakes in the Kansai region, citizens and local government tended to be unaware of this possibility 10 years ago.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: The death and destruction caused by the quake gave a serious shock to the city's residents.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: One story of the Kobe city hall was totally destroyed, and a part of Meishin Highway between Nagoya and Kobe was ripped apart; a bus barely avoided falling from the broken highway.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Engineers buttressed vulnerable city structures throughout Japan after the earthquake.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Research revealed that architecture designed under national earthquake-proof standards had survived the earthquake.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Many old buildings were rebuilt, reconstructed, or given structual support.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Vulnerable city infrastructure was also attended to; in some areas water and fuel supply had been disrupted for over two months.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Many municipalities reviewed their standards for civil engineering design.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: The earthquake also revealed systematic vulnerability within the Japanese government.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: The prime minister at that time, Tomiichi Murayama, first learned of the earthquake from a TV news program two hours later, and not from a government report.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: He called his secretary, who also knew nothing of it.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: The government improved these weaknesses, and in the case of the Chuetsu Earthquake in October 2004, the prime minister's office was able to quickly deal with the accident.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: After the earthquake, many people spent days in shelters.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: 104,900 houses were completely destroyed, and 144,256 only partly desroyed.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: The Hyogo prefecture and municipalities provided temporary shelters, called Kasetsujutaku.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Such temporary houses had remained since 2000.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Since those houses were provided to individuals and not to communities, many people found they were no longer with their familiar neighbors after moving.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: This caused serious problems among people, especially the elderly.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Since 2000, around 200 people have died alone in such temporary houses, to be found only days later; this was considered a serious social problem.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: A word was even coined for this situation, Kodokushi (meaning "death in solitude" in Japanese), but some say no effective solution has yet been offered.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: The earthquake has also had a bright side.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Before the earthquake, it was not popular to participate voluntarily in social activities in Japan.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: The earthquake moved many people to join such activities.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Since it was close to the end of the Japanese schoolyear, many students could stay in the affected area for long days.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: And it has been not easy to have a vacation for Japanese workers, as many people took vacations from their company and went to the affected area to help out.
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: This was not just a temporary movement, but influenced people to consider such social engagement as a regular activity (one can see a similar influcence in the case of the Chuetsu Earthquake).
title: Kobe commemorates earthquake victims

text: Investigators examining the wreck of British Airways Flight 38, a Boeing 777 that crash landed short of the runway at London's Heathrow Airport in the first hull loss of a 777, are examining the aircraft's fuel system as a possible factor in the crash.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: No-one was killed as the scheduled flight from Beijing, China lost power during final approach on January 17.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: 136 passengers and 16 crew were on board when power was lost to the two Rolls-Royce engines about two miles from the runway, at a height of 600 feet.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: Autopilot and autothrottle were engaged at the time, the latter having just commanded an increase of thrust to the engines when power was lost.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: Co-pilot John Coward, in control at the time, was subsequently praised for being able to glide the disabled plane to within 1,000 feet of the runway, clearing a number of houses along the way.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: Subsequent investigation has revealed that not only did the engines not fail simultaneously, but neither failed completely, contradicting initial belief.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: A preliminary report by the United Kingdom's Aircraft Accident Investigation Branch (AAIB) stated that after the autothrottle commanded more thrust "The engines both initially responded but after about 3 seconds the thrust of the right engine reduced.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: Some eight seconds later the thrust reduced on the left engine to a similar level...
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: Both engines continued to produce thrust at an engine speed above flight idle, but less than the commanded thrust."
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: This situation prevailed until impact.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: On Wednesday the AAIB stated that they were examining "All possible scenarios that could explain the thrust reduction and continued lack of response of the engines."
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: However, it also went on to specifically mention attention to the jet's fuel system, saying "This work includes a detailed analysis and examination of the complete fuel-flow path from the aircraft tanks to the engine-fuel nozzles."
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: The AAIB also ruled out the plane having completely run out of fuel, stating that there was "adequate fuel" in the tanks when the plane crashed.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: In addition to the fuel required to get to the target destination or emergency alternative airport - whichever is further - aircraft typically carry between thirty and forty-five minutes worth of extra fuel as a safety margin.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: Possible scenarios being examined include fuel contamination, coming either from fuel taken on at Beijing or leakage from an unknown source.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: In particular, a heavy contaminant at the bottom of the tanks would explain a lack of earlier problems on the flight, as the fuel levels would only have become low in the final stages of the trip.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: Another possibility is that a central part of the fuel system developed a leak, reducing the amount of fuel available to the engines.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: It is known that, according to the AAIB, "the autothrottle and engine-control commands were performing as expected prior to, and after, the reduction in thrust," suggesting that all software in the aircraft was functioning correctly and rendering a software failure unlikely, although this possibility also remains under investigation.
title: British Airways Flight 38 investigation focuses on fuel system

text: A University of Calgary research team developed a new method for extracting carbon dioxide (CO2) directly from the air — a fundamental shift in carbon capture technology enabling capture of the most common greenhouse gas from so-called diffuse sources like aircraft, trucks and automobiles that represent half of the greenhouse gases emitted globally.
title: University of Calgary scientist Keith cracks carbon capture conundrum

text: Professor David Keith, Director of University of Calgary's (UofC) Institute for Sustainable Energy, Environment and Economy (ISEEE) and a team of researchers from UofC's Energy and Environmental Systems Group built and operated a prototype system this summer producing results that compared favourably with commercial carbon capture systems.
title: University of Calgary scientist Keith cracks carbon capture conundrum

text: Two 'provisional' patents have been filed on the technology but Keith warns there are still "many pitfalls along the path to commercialization."
title: University of Calgary scientist Keith cracks carbon capture conundrum

text: Using a process adapted from the pulp-and-paper industry that halves the cost of CO2 air capture in their custom-built tower, Professor Keith and his team captured the equivalent of about 20 tonnes per year of CO2 (approximately equal to the yearly output of one person in North America) directly from the air with less than 100 kilowatt-hours of electricity per tonne of carbon dioxide on a single square metre of scrubbing material.
title: University of Calgary scientist Keith cracks carbon capture conundrum

text: "This means that if you used electricity from a coal-fired power plant, for every unit of electricity you used to operate the capture machine, you'd be capturing 10 times as much CO2 as the power plant emitted making that much electricity," explains Professor Keith.
title: University of Calgary scientist Keith cracks carbon capture conundrum

text: A report co-authored by Keith in the American Chemical Society's journal Environmental Science & Technology explains "nearly all current research on carbon capture and storage (CCS) focuses on capturing CO2 from large, stationary sources such as power plants.
title: University of Calgary scientist Keith cracks carbon capture conundrum

text: Such plans usually entail separating CO2 from flue gas, compressing it, and transporting it via pipeline to be [stored] underground."
title: University of Calgary scientist Keith cracks carbon capture conundrum

text: Using CO2 air capture technology, "a company could, in principle, contract with an oil sands plant near Fort McMurray to remove CO2 from the air and could build its air capture plant wherever it's cheapest — China, for example — and the same amount of CO2 would be removed," says Professor Keith in a UofC press release.
title: University of Calgary scientist Keith cracks carbon capture conundrum

text: "While it's important to get started doing things we know how to do, like wind power, nuclear power, and 'regular' carbon capture and storage," Professor Keith continues, "it's also vital to start thinking about radical new ideas and approaches to solving this problem."
title: University of Calgary scientist Keith cracks carbon capture conundrum

text: ISEEE's Executive Director David Layzell points out that "energy-efficient and cost-effective air capture could play a valuable role in complementing other approaches for reducing emissions from the transportation sector, such as biofuels or electric vehicles."
title: University of Calgary scientist Keith cracks carbon capture conundrum

text: Wednesday, a team of researchers at the University of East Anglia, Norwich, United Kingdom published a study of the increasing deer population in the United Kingdom, in the Journal of Wildlife Management.

text: In a first ever effort in the United States to eliminate the presence of Zebra mussels in a large body of water, the Virginia Department of Game and Inland Fisheries (VDGIF) announced on Monday that a private pond in Prince William County, Virginia is undergoing water treatment using a chemical potash of potassium chloride in concentrations high enough to kill invasive and native shellfish species.

text: There are no expected health risks for humans, or contamination of drinking water wells in the immediate vicinity.

text: Bottom-dwelling marine species are often covered by the Zebra Mussel.

title: Virginia takes action against Zebra Mussels in private pond

text: In Maryland, boat owners who launch water craft on reservoirs that serve as sources of drinking water are required to register their boat for use only on those reservoirs, to reduce chances of the mussel being transferred from other waters.
title: Virginia takes action against Zebra Mussels in private pond

text: Drinking water treatment and power production facilities where the mussels are present must regularly treat their systems to keep them clear of decaying debris that fouls intake pipes.
title: Virginia takes action against Zebra Mussels in private pond

text: Zebra mussels were first discovered in North America in 1988, in Lake Saint Clair, a lake between Lake Erie and Lake Huron.
title: Virginia takes action against Zebra Mussels in private pond

title: Virginia takes action against Zebra Mussels in private pond

text: A report by the British Health and Safety Executive (HSE) into the Buncefield oil depot fire of December 2005 has suggested that an oil tank at the site was overflowing for 40 minutes before the first explosion took place.

text: It is not known for certain what caused the spark that led to the first explosion.
title: Buncefield oil depot tank 'was overflowing'

text: Any evidence is likely to have been destroyed in the fire, and so the exact cause may never be known.
title: Buncefield oil depot tank 'was overflowing'

title: Buncefield oil depot tank 'was overflowing'

text: U.S. President George W. Bush yesterday signed an executive order declaring the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a U.S. National Monument, creating the largest protected marine area in the world and the largest single conservation area in the history of the United States.
title: Bush proclaims Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a National Monument

text: In a signing ceremony attended by Hawaii officials, including Hawaii Governor Linda Lingle, Bush pledged, "This region holds the largest and healthiest untouched coral reef system in the United States.

text: And we're going to preserve it."

text: Bush reportedly moved quickly to protect the archipelago after a screening of Jean-Michel Cousteau's documentary Voyage to Kure in April.

text: He invoked powers under the Antiquities Act of 1906, which gives the President the power to restrict the use of public land by executive order.

title: Bush proclaims Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a National Monument

text: As a National Monument, the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands would be subject to one of the highest levels of protection in the U.S. All fishing will be phased out over five years, and visitors will require permits for snorkeling and diving.
title: Bush proclaims Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a National Monument

text: Lingle had enacted similar protections as Hawaii governor, but the protections were limited to a three-mile radius from shore.
title: Bush proclaims Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a National Monument

text: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration would manage the monument along with its 13 national marine sanctuaries.
title: Bush proclaims Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a National Monument

text: Advocates for the fishing industry have raised concerns about the feasibility of further protections, asserting that a small fishery operation in the area would cause little environmental impact.
title: Bush proclaims Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a National Monument

text: Kitty Simonds of the Western Pacific Regional Fishery Management Council said, "The President can do whatever he wants to do, but we're disappointed that we can't continue on a small, healthy bottomfish fishery."
title: Bush proclaims Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a National Monument

text: Environmental groups generally lauded Bush's move.
title: Bush proclaims Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a National Monument

text: "When you add it all up, it's a world-class ecological jewel.
title: Bush proclaims Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a National Monument

text: From both a national and global perspective, this really is a landmark conservation event," said Joshua Reichert, head of the environment program for the private Pew Charitable Trusts.
title: Bush proclaims Northwestern Hawaiian Islands a National Monument

text: The preserve, covering all the islands northwest of Niihau, covers 140,000 square miles (360,000 km²), covering 10 islands and atolls, and stretches for about 1,400 miles (2,200 km).
